advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the drain-lock reclaim (stamped_file_is_stale -> unlink) cannot break a newly-acquired live lock in the TOCTOU window, given there is no fcntl exclusion here as there is for the mkdir leg.
evidence: lock_owner._stamp_is_stale relies on fcntl proof for the mkdir leg: src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:360-366 'A live owner inside its own hold would still hold that fcntl leg, so we could not have acquired it and could not be here.'

stamped_file_is_stale always passes fcntl_held=False (src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:275), so the drain lock has no equivalent exclusion — the stale-check-then-unlink window is a TOCTOU where a newly-acquired live lock can be unlinked.
advisory.finding: The drain-lock reclaim path (stamped_file_is_stale -> os.unlink) holds no exclusion between the staleness check and the unlink, unlike the mkdir leg which the shared _stamp_is_stale docstring documents as safe only because the caller holds the exclusive fcntl leg for the whole hold. A drainer that released after the stale check but before the unlink can be replaced by a fresh, live, correctly-stamped drainer whose lock is then unlinked, so two drainers proceed and a live holder's lock is broken — contradicting the 'a live drainer is never broken' claim in the docstrings.
scenarios: A stale (dead-pid) drain lock is detected; before the unlink, another drainer acquires and stamps a fresh live lock; the reclaimer unlinks the live drainer's lock and both drain concurrently.

scenarios: A drain lock with a truncated v2 stamp is logged as 'unstamped' by the WARNING skip line but shown as 'incomplete ownership stamp' by doctor, confusing an operator correlating the two.

advisory.finding: The drain-lock row's two non-empty holder_description branches added by this diff — 'unknown (unrecognised ownership stamp)' when _parse_v2_stamp returns None on non-empty content, and 'unknown (incomplete ownership stamp)' when a v2 stamp is missing fields — are untested. The new drain-lock tests only plant an EMPTY stamp ('no ownership stamp') or valid v2 stamps; a regression that mis-routed a torn or non-v2 drain stamp (e.g. mislabelling it, or crashing on the incomplete case) would not be caught. The analogous mkdir-leg test exists (test_an_unrecognised_stamp_is_stated_not_guessed) but exercises different code (LEG_TICKETS_MKDIR).
